neighbours.label: ' of' inside a fixed multiword name or term where the phrase is a set expression (Table of Contents, Prisoners of War, schools of thought, activities of daily living)
fire: Please check the Table of Contents before you start reading the manual.
The Geneva Conventions protect Prisoners of War held by either side.
Philosophers from different schools of thought disagree on this question.
Therapists assess activities of daily living such as bathing and dressing.
He was named Chief of Staff shortly after the election.
The company changed its Terms of Service again this month.
She studied the Bill of Rights in her first year of law school.
The guide lists the Wonders of the World in order of age.
quiet: Please check the color of the cover before you order the manual.
The guards gave a bowl of rice to each person held by either side.
Philosophers from different parts of the country disagree on this question.
Therapists assess the height of the bed and the width of the door.
He was given a pile of letters shortly after the election.
The company changed the layout of its office again this month.
She studied the history of her town in her first year of school.
The guide lists the rooms of the house in order of size.

notes: 16 of the top 32 peak on ' of', but the pole is sparse (0.04%), so ordinary 'of' must stay quiet. Near misses use 'of' in free, compositional phrases.
